newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India sells 25,000/t September naphtha to Stinnes.
newsitem.headline: India sells 25,000/t September naphtha to Stinnes.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has sold through a tender 25,000 tonnes of naphtha to German trader Stinnes at $25.84 per tonne below Northwest European (NWE) quotes spot on a free-on-board basis, traders said on Monday.
IOC offered the 25,000 tonnes of high aromatic naphtha lifting from Bombay on the west coast between September 27-29 in a tender which closed on September 12 and which was valid until September 13.
Traders said the cargo was awarded to the U.S. affiliate of the German trader as the cargo was more likely to head to the stronger western markets.
Asian naphtha demand has been dampened by petrochemical shutdowns in northern Asia in October and November, traders said.
The last high aromatic cargo sold out of Bombay, which lifted between September 11-12, was at a slightly firmer price of $23.34 below NWE quotes.
